Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.

to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-

sampling context together.

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is hydrocodone, a 4,5-epoxymorphinan; the closest no-external-condition morphinan context, samidorphan, has absolute oral bioavailability of 69% (range 60.3–82.6%), well above the 20% threshold.
Other opioid/morphinan contexts report F above threshold: pentazocine 0.68–0.70 in cirrhosis, pethidine 0.80 in cirrhosis, and morphine 27.7–124% in cirrhosis.

L4 and L5 absorption/efflux evidence for related morphinans supports a favorable absorption component: codeine has high Caco-2 and small-intestinal permeability similar to metoprolol, dextromethorphan is almost completely absorbed, morphine is rapidly absorbed from the small intestine, a codeine analog has high MDCK-MDR1 permeability, buprenorphine has high permeability, and (-)-SPD shows passive diffusion with efflux ratio 1.0.
No transferable affirmative low-F evidence is present; the only low record (rat S-RCP 17%) is a different benzamide scaffold and does not support F < 20% for the query.

evidence_gaps: No direct hydrocodone-specific absolute oral bioavailability record is present in the supplied cards.

L5 gut-wall efflux/intestinal-metabolism records are for related morphinans (morphine, codeine analog, buprenorphine, (-)-SPD), not hydrocodone itself; no direct intestinal metabolism or efflux measurement for the query is available.
No IV-matched oral exposure for hydrocodone is provided, so first-pass metabolism is not directly quantified.
Most structurally similar opioid F records come from cirrhotic patients, where first-pass extraction may be reduced; healthy-subject F for the query may differ.
No transferable affirmative low-F evidence is available; the only low record is rat S-RCP (17%), which is not applicable.
